text:
alex: heads-up — noticed a handful of entries in the console ledger where a streaming session that reconnected after a prefetch cutoff got billed for the toolcall tokens twice. not a huge spike but reproducible on my dev tenant.

maya: hmm. prefetch cutoff as in the server trimmed the active KV cache and resumed from client snapshot?

alex: yeah. client reconnects, server serves cached prefetched tokens for the prefix, then we fire a toolcall for the suffix. on reconnect path the tooling trace shows a short TTL for the toolcall and the billing delta shows both the prefetched chunk and the subsequent toolcall tokens counted separately.

sam: can you paste the simplified trace (ids masked) and the ledger rows? even a small snippet helps.

alex: sure — gist:```
TRACE: session=svc-xx reconnect ts=2026-03-19T10:04:12Z
RECV: prefix chunk (prefetch hit) token_count=18
SEND: toolcall id=tc-yy ttl=3 tokens=22
LEDGER rows:
  prefetched_token_row: session=svc-xx tokens=18 reason=prefetch
  toolcall_token_row: session=svc-xx tokens=22 reason=toolcall
```

maya: do we currently attribute prefetched fragments to an optimistic provisional bucket until the session confirms? or do we commit immediately on send?

sam: quick answer — prefetch counts are currently committed on serve (immediate) but flagged provisional=true in the ledger for a grace window. toolcalls always commit confirmed. we later reconcile provisional rows.

jen: so the double-count is possible if reconciliation doesn't find the prefetched row tied to the later toolcall. why wouldn't it? is the session id different across reconnects?

alex: session id is the same, but the toolcall has a different ephemeral call id. reconciliation matches by prefix hash + session id. in this repro the prefix hash differs by one char because client truncated trailing whitespace on reconnect (weird).

liam: whitespace normalization :facepalm:. Can we normalize prefix canonicalization at the router level before ledger emission? That would avoid relying on client idempotency.

maya: agreed, but we need to be careful — canonicalization changes unit economics slightly (e.g., preserving/stripping newline changes tokenization). might affect analytics & SLOs.

sam: for immediate mitigation: mark prefetched provisional rows with an attached resume_window_id emitted by runtime on resume. then reconciliation can match on resume_window_id + session id even if prefix hashes drift. cheap change?

alex: that would work. resume_window_id is already in traces but not emitted to the ledger currently. patch proposal: router includes resume_window_id in ledger rows for provisional prefetch.

jen: +1. how does this interact with the console UX? ops will see provisional rows with resume_window_id; we should show a join view that groups provisional + confirmed by resume_window_id so it looks like one logical charge.

liam: console-side group view makes sense. also add a small note in the billing tooltip: "prefetch rows may be reconciled with subsequent toolcalls during a short grace window".

maya: long-term: consider canonicalizing prefixes in the runtime and moving canonicalization rules into a stable config so product teams can opt in/out. that prevents tokenization-based edgecases.

sam: ok action items: (1) eng-runtime: add resume_window_id to provisional prefetch ledger rows (PR incoming), (2) eng-platform: console group-by-resume_window_id and tooltip text, (3) billing: run a one-off reconcile to dedupe past suspected duplicates (query by session + proximate timestamps and similar token counts).

alex: filing a short replay script and attaching example session ids in the bug. will tag PRs. thanks folks :)

billing-bot: scheduled job started: historical-dedupe-run 2026-03-19T14:00:00Z (eta 20m) :gear:
